changes.after:
## Deliverables
1. Implement SQLite's share of the one shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its single AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) operation for several row operations as one atomic unit; SQLite (d-6), Postgres (d-7) and MySQL (d-8) each implement that same contract (ANC-032/033). Implement the shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its generic transaction operation that runs several row operations as one atomic unit over a bounded channel whose design is adapted from atm-core (copied code, no dependency), single writer and reader pool. The writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; reader workers open read-only connections. Futures are NEW work, not copied typed operations. Read-write body is one writer message/savepoint; queue batches commit together and replies follow commit. Read-only may use reader pool — REQ-DBSQ-0002/0003; ANC-022..027/033.
2. Enforce transaction-body non-suspension: Pending rolls back with typed error, failed/panicked body never commits. Public storage APIs return typed Result and never panic; writer panic terminates/fails every pending/in-flight/queued caller without hangs — NFR-RUN-0002; ANC-035/036. Qualify actual external analyzer/no-panic rules for changed code, never substitute runtime polling for static analysis.
3. Generic row/migration/codec implementation contains no cron/application table type, schema or SQL. Consumer supplies row descriptors; all consumer policies live above storage. No sc-cron dependency/feature — ANC-032/034. Consume real row/options/codec declarations frozen in d-5; implement the concrete database API, with no duplicate definitions.
4. Use the shared root rusqlite requirement >=0.41 with no upper bound; run the normal SQLite test suite. Thin generated SQLite storage consumes the generic backend and application-owned schema and removes SQLx SQLite/cache/config — REQ-DBSQ-0001; REQ-RUN-0308; ANC-012/028/037.

5. Retire the public raw-SQL SqliteWriter/WriterConn/SqlValue/SqliteWriterError facade in0.3.0; raw connection/execute helpers become crate-private behind generic Storage<T>. Implement inherent SqliteDatabase open/storage/shutdown/wait_closed with SqliteOpenOptions, not a factory trait. Amend REQ-DBSQ-0001/0002 and its architecture/boundary public facade to the final implemented dependency/API surface, following d-5 declarations. All owned registry requirements use >= tested floors without upper bounds (ANC-037).

## Boundaries and handoffs
Cron schema/domain policy/migration are d-9; real cron conformance and complete generated/mixed layouts are d-11; actual upstream/publication d-12. Backend tests use generic rows and do not contain a CronRow codec or cron SQL.
This sprint implements Storage<T> for SqliteStore<T> using that shared trait, with no SQLite-specific parallel storage trait; it implements the SAME AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) method as one writer message/savepoint.
After the d-5 boundary registration handoff, own boundaries/sc-runtime-db-sqlite/sc-runtime-db-sqlite.toml for the actual public-facade/root removals matching this implementation. This is the boundary's own facade, not a shared root registry.

changes.after:
## Deliverables
1. Implement MySQL's share of the one shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its single AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) operation for several row operations as one atomic unit; SQLite (d-6), Postgres (d-7) and MySQL (d-8) each implement that same contract (ANC-032/033). Implement MysqlStore<T>: sc-storage Storage<T> plus the same generic AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer), generic row mapping, generated-key insert/delete and engine factory. App owns schema/migrations; no WidgetRow, CronRow or consumer SQL lives in the generic engine (ANC-032/033/034/035).
2. Replace the sqlx umbrella with sqlx-core/sqlx-mysql/sqlx-macros >=0.9, no upper bound. Qualify real live query macros, migrations/offline replacement and CLI paths, preserving typed errors and existing wrapper behavior (REQ-RUN-0002/0302/0321; ANC-037).
3. Bound serialization retries and pool-acquire/statement/transaction waits in EngineConfig using finite defaults and validated configuration. Exhaustion/deadline yields typed StorageError with retryability/recovery, never an infinite loop. Controlled conflicts/timeouts test the bound; no sleeps or load races. Retry knobs are engine policy, not extra transaction properties (NFR-RUN-0002/0009).

## This sprint does not close
Real production composition, generated database security and registry migration are d-11; no generator/sync/permission feature is added.

Implement only the domain CronStorage surface; keep the underlying Storage<CronRow> backend private and map its typed failures to CronError. 2. Migrate scheduler/worker to awaited app-supplied storage, preserving hooks/Monty, clocks, in-flight skip, cooperative cancellation and typed FENCED behavior. Domain read/check/mutate runs in one serializable atomic body, never separate calls. Backend is table-neutral — ADR-RUN-0013/0014/0020.
3. Implement legacy cron.db-to-app-DB migration above generic storage: preserve IDs/generation/run/end/spec/hook state; idempotent import and collision/rollback refusal. Legacy source is read only as explicit migration input, no ongoing second database setting — REQ-CRON-0004.

Retire legacy DB files/dependency only after generic suite has equivalent case IDs and double tests pass. Actual engine/two-process provider runs are d-11, not a false double claim. Adapt thin cron-command APIs and READMEs — REQ-RUN-0702; ANC-012/035.


## Boundaries and handoffs
Full real-SQLite/mixed-engine cron conformance is d-11, actual released beads-cache d-12. No storage backend imports sc-cron or specific table code. No separate duplicate cron invariant suite.
CronStore consumes AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) from the shared Storage<T> contract; d-6/d-7/d-8 implement that same method for SQLite/Postgres/MySQL, while d-9 supplies only cron policy bodies (ANC-033).
Retire ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and legacy SQLite files in0.3.0, updating lib.rs/row.rs/storage.rs after the d-5 handoff. CronStore wraps Storage<CronRow> privately and exposes only policy-checked CronStorage operations. Keep per-name in-flight behavior and generation fencing under local REQ-CRON-0001 and ADR-RUN-0013; upstream crosswalk numbers are provenance, not local requirement IDs.
Convert every remaining registry line in crates/sc-cron/Cargo.toml and every registry line in crates/sc-cron-commands/Cargo.toml, including dev/optional entries, to >= tested floors with no upper bound; preserve features. This includes async-trait, chrono, cron, getrandom, tokio, tracing, process-wrap, monty, monty-types, tempfile and libc, plus utoipa >=6.0.0 and schemars >=1.2.3 in sc-cron-commands (ANC-037). boundary:template-service — service tests cover real common write/read and Python/Monty transform execution against the contract storage double; typed errors and existing DTO behavior hold; no unfinished branch. Run generated service crate tests/lints and workspace/boundary validation under the configured generation harness. This does not claim production database, transport or release integration; d-11 owns those.

## Required validation commands
Generate a development-source consumer using just new <temp-dir> --var-file wizard/fixtures/postgres.json (no cron selected). Run cargo test --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml and cargo clippy --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings with required interpreter prerequisites; service contract tests use the controlled storage double and actual Python/Monty transform execution. Then build the generated workspace and run its configured sc-boundary profile. Existing legacy wrappers keep unrelated consumer code compiling until d-11 wiring; no live database or transport proof is claimed here.
Run cargo test -p sc-command --test storage_combinators with the real default combinators and controlled storage/transform errors; no per-app duplicate generic pipeline. No ATM/sc-compose or SQLx dependency in the shared storage/command seam.
boundary:template-service/preserved-crud — Existing create/get/delete/row-delete service behavior, generated IDs and typed errors are unchanged against shared double; default helper implementation/exports and README match the real sc-storage trait. Implement the d-5-frozen, owner-ratified option (a) extension with no operation removal.
boundary:template-service/nonblocking — On a controlled single-thread runtime, interpreter worker signals entered then holds on a barrier. While held, an independent async task completes/acknowledges; only that acknowledgment releases the worker. Both success and panic map to typed Results; no sleeps, elapsed deadlines or load races establish correctness. Test cancellation/channel closure deterministically. Storage submission is never wrapped in spawn_blocking. cargo build --workspace passes at closure.
boundary:template-service/transform-limits — Before spawn_blocking, acquire a bounded transform permit or return a typed saturation error. Hold that permit until the worker actually exits, including caller cancellation. Apply the published Monty resource/deadline limits to computation itself, map expiry/errors/panic to typed transform errors, and test expiry/saturation/cancellation with controlled inputs. Timing out the JoinHandle alone is not termination proof.

Consumes d-3's compiled sc-command server/schema/envelope/error implementation with rmcp>=3.9 and matching registry identities, plus d-5 Storage/row contracts.
Its storage/mapping/error/extension contract comes from d-5. The service boundary owns typed command/transform behavior and can be tested independently with the contract double, not actual engine implementation. Proposed flow:
write: decode Tcli -> await app transform(Tcli)->Tsql -> await storage.write(&row) -> existing envelope/error projection;
read: await storage.read(key)->Option<Tsql> -> await app transform(Tsql)->Tcli -> existing envelope/error projection.
Preserve the existing public widget DTO/error contract unless explicitly changed in d-5. Python/Monty function execution is real in service tests, storage is the controlled test double. No generator, registry or specified permission policy is added. Daemon/CLI/wizard wiring belongs to d-11, backend row codecs to d-6/7/8. Use the published Monty interpreter directly; preserve existing cron hook code.

Consumes real d-5 sc-storage Storage/row signatures; implement them once in sc-command/src/storage.rs, exported with the actual implementation. Application service supplies Tcli/Tsql transforms, including real Python/Monty execution, and uses controlled Storage<T> double. No runtime block_on/Handle/futures bridge or sleep in production. Service boundary manifests are generated by d-5 renderer at boundaries/<prefixed-service>/<prefixed-service>.toml; criteria target that emitted boundary/ADR0021.
Interpreter mechanism: tokio::task::spawn_blocking for synchronous Monty/Python evaluation, using published Monty ResourceLimits/ResourceTracker with the existing bounded feed pattern. It is explicitly allowed for interpreter execution, never to submit/wait for SQLite storage. Transform::apply awaits the JoinHandle and maps interpreter error/panic to typed transform error; no block_on or sleep. Transaction bodies may not call this mechanism or await interpreter/I/O; transformation completes before entering named atomic storage.
Use schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, WidgetStorage extension and StoresView exact contracts. Preserve CreateWidget/GetWidget/DeleteWidget/DeleteRow DTO behavior and error codes against the shared double, including store-generated IDs. Common functions consume the real sc-storage Storage<T>/atomic contracts; Transform and command errors are local sc-command types. Consume the option (a) extension frozen and ratified at d-5 closure.
Own the WidgetStore<S> application wrapper over generic Storage<schema::WidgetRow>: map typed errors to existing StoreError, implement WidgetStorage/StoresView and preserve create-with-generated-id/get/delete. The per-layout application factory translates schema::OpenConfig to table-neutral engine config; d-11 injects concrete stores. No table-specific widget code is placed in generic engine crates.
Transform hosting uses the existing published monty ResourceLimits/ResourceTracker APIs directly, including the maximum feed duration pattern already used by sc-cron. Service code is only its application-specific input/output and bounded blocking adapter; do not copy the scheduler feed/session/host machinery or add a sc-cron dependency to no-cron layouts. sc-cron retains its scheduler-specific host. Generic command composition is two free async functions in sc-command; Transform is intentionally open for application implementations.

Public API shape: storage_write(store, transform, input) and storage_read(store, transform, key) are plain generic async functions returning typed StorageCommandError; no DefaultStorageCommands type.
